title: Texas True Crime: Til Death Do Us Part
text:
TEXAS TRUE CRIME: On December 23, 2012, Jaime and Sandra Melgar were celebrating their 32nd wedding anniversary. But the night went horribly wrong - and the next day, Jaime Melgar was found dead.
What began as a celebration of a wedding anniversary ended in tragedy for Houston couple Sandra and Jaime "Jim" Melgar, a case that led to a murder conviction and an ongoing legal fight that continues years later.
Sandra and Jaime Melgar, high school sweethearts who met as teenagers at Lamar High School in Houston, had been married for 32 years. They built what family members described as a typical suburban life, with Jim working while Sandy focused on raising their daughter, Lizz Rose. On Dec. 22, 2012, the couple celebrated their anniversary with dinner at their favorite Mexican restaurant, Los Cucos, before returning home.
"It was undisputed that they had taken a bath together after they got home. They spent a number of hours in the bath. There were some sex toys found in and around that area," Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare said about that night. At the time, the couple's daughter was living in England and was unaware anything had happened until she began receiving messages a day later, on social media.
"I was getting all these messages from my friends, they were all telling me they loved me, that they were there for me, and call them and get in touch. I thought it must have something to do with my hospital stay. But then somebody else got in touch and sent me a link to a news story. That's basically how I was told something horrible had happened.
I didn't know what, but I knew my dad was dead. I had to get home," Rose said. Investigators later determined that Jim Melgar had been stabbed multiple times and was found inside a closet in the family's home. Sandra Melgar was found unharmed and tied up in a different closet.
Melgar told investigators that she had blacked out during a home robbery. Authorities, however, believed she had staged the scene. During a police interrogation that was conducted soon after Jaime was found dead, detectives repeatedly questioned her account.
"I wouldn't even know where to start to stage it. And how am I going to tie myself up like that and not even be able to get out of it?
"The investigation continued for years. More than two years passed before Sandra Melgar was indicted, and another three years elapsed before the case went to trial. In 2017, a jury found Melgar guilty of murdering her husband.
"I think it was just complete shock. I feel like I went numb and like everything just went quiet and I was just sitting there and I had like a ringing in my ears and I knew everything was going on around me. It just felt like an out of body experience. I don't know.
It was, um, traumatic," Rose said of the verdict. Melgar was sentenced to 27 years in prison. But her family and supporters have continued fighting to overturn the conviction, with much of that effort led by Rose. Their hopes now rest with the Innocence Project of Texas, which has taken up the case.
"Well, certainly when we file the writ, we know they're innocent, you know, uh, otherwise we don't file the writ. We know they're innocent now, you know, uh, convincing the judge, um, is, is what our job is," said Mike Ware of the Innocence Project of Texas. Ware is now leading the legal efforts to get Sandra Melgar a new trial.
The appellate case remains before the courts, while questions persist among Melgar's supporters about whether the right person was convicted and whether those responsible for Jaime Melgar's death have been identified. For Rose, the effort to clear her mother's name has become a central part of her life.
"It's kind of taken over my life now. It's become a full-time job. But it'll be worth it if in the end my mom gets to come home," she said. In our newest episode of Texas True Crime, 'Til Death Do Us Part', ABC13's Miya Shay speaks to people involved on both sides of the case, as Sandra Melgar remains behind bars.

The couple married in a romantic woodland setting with bride Sally, 42, wowing in an off-the-shoulder gown with a split, while Rufus, 47, sported a dark green suit. Writing on X, he said: 'In the past two years sallyhodgkiss has redefined how completely loved or seen I ever believed someone could make me feel. 'We talk and nourish each other in a way that's almost unbelievable to me. Last night, I asked her to marry me.' Describing the moment, Rufus said: 'We were privileged enough to take part in theimprovathon WiltonMusicHall, a show in which brilliant, erudite, playful, thoughtful, beautiful, sleep deprived people spoke repeatedly of love, commitment, joy and demonstrated the awesome magic that comes when such people do so.' He said: 'Sally walked down for her final bow. As she spoke - a poetic, magnificent final flourish - the universe seemed to scream at me that the time - bizarre as it might be- had come. 'As the crowd applauded her, I took to the stage beside her. Wordlessly, I mimed that I was unlikely to be able to speak, as I was totally overwhelmed. 'Then I dropped to one knee and she looked confused - this would be an odd twist for the characters we'd been playing (siblings as they were). It was only when I spoke her name she realised what was happening. Some people took pictures. 'She said yes. My kids are f***ing delighted, my ex congratulated me on the news, my parents are beside themselves and my best friend Steve contacted a special Wedding Robot for validation.'
